newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong steps up Vietnam boatpeople repatriation.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong steps up Vietnam boatpeople repatriation.

text.p: Hong Kong repatriated a record 709 Vietnamese boatpeople on Thursday in its drive to clear failed asylum seekers from the British colony before China takes over next July.
The operation, the largest single-day repatriation ever organised, involved four morning flights to Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, the office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said.
The departures were organised under a UNHCR-supervised voluntary repatriation programme for boatpeople who have failed to win international refugee status.
The programme has sent back 8,140 Vietnamese this year. The Hong Kong government operates a parallel programme of mandatory repatriation.
The latest returns reduced the Vietnamese population in Hong Kong's tense detention centres to 6,274, down from a high of more than 42,000 recorded in late 1992, the UNHCR said.

The detainees are the last of a tidal wave of refugees who fled from Vietnam, many by boat, after the communists won the war there in 1975. Hong Kong's camps were rocked by fierce riots this year when Vietnamese attempted mass escapes.
China has insisted that all the Vietnamese be gone from Hong Kong when London hands the colony back to Beijing at midnight next June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule.
